reason: No PO class exists for intersecondary veins. They are neither secondary nor tertiary veins, so mapping to the parent leaf lamina vein is correct and follows the earlier rules for basal vein and veinlet.

A secretory canal is a tube-shaped space lined by secretory cells, so its counts, lines and visibility belong to a canal, not to secretory tissue. PO canal is a groove or internal tube. Resin canal (PO_0005665) is only right where the secretion is stated to be resin.
Plural of secretory canal; same reasoning as R2495.
French for secretory canal; same reasoning as R2495.
French plural of secretory canal; same reasoning as R2495.
A secretory duct is the same structure as a secretory canal (a tube-shaped space). The PO canal class fits better than the tissue.

PO's note on alar cell only says the area they form is sometimes called the alar region. The region's size and shape (triangular, reaching the margin) are not the size or shape of one alar cell. This needs a region or cell-group class, not a single-cell mapping.
An alar group is a group of cells. Its size and shape would wrongly be given to single alar cells, and there is no class for the group.
An alar area is a region of the leaf base. Same problem as R2501.

PO already lists 'head' as a synonym of capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030121) with no limit, and the 2026-11-13 review mapped 'head' the same way (C262). The first check's limits are family names, which the part-name limit field cannot use.

In these floras, brood bodies are the many-celled asexual propagules of bryophytes, which are gemmae. Family or group names cannot be used as a part-name limit, and flowering-plant bulbils are called bulbils, which maps to aerial tuber (PO_0004548).
Plural of R2507; same reasoning.

A bamboo culm sheath is the sheath of a culm leaf, so it is a leaf sheath of a modified leaf. Its hairs, colour and texture are sheath qualities. The first check was wrong to say it is not a leaf sheath.
Plural of R2509; same reasoning.
A median vein is a leaf midvein only on leaves and leaflets. On bracts, lemmas or sepals it is another organ's vein and must not become a leaf midvein.
Bare 'médiane' is an adjective (median lobe, tooth, sepal). 'nervure médiane' already has its own rule (R2304), so this bare word is not needed.

A pseudostyle (Schisandraceae, some Annonaceae) is a sterile extension of the carpel, not a style. Mapping it to style gives it a wrong meaning, and carpel would wrongly receive its length. It needs its own class.
Plural of R2513; same reasoning.
Primary divisions are pinnae only for compound leaves and fronds. For a calyx, corolla or inflorescence they are lobes or branches.
Plural of R2518; same limit.
French form of R2518; same limit, using the French and English part names.

A false panicle is the whole inflorescence and is not a true panicle (PO_0030123). The general inflorescence class is correct, and its qualities belong to the inflorescence. This follows the accepted fallback to the parent class.
French form of R2524; same reasoning.

The Andropogoneae spatheate compound panicle is the whole inflorescence. Mapping to inflorescence is correct, and the spathe can be annotated separately (spathe is an inflorescence bract synonym in PO).
'Propagula' is the Latin-style plural used for bryophyte asexual propagules, and the examples are bryophytes. Family or group names cannot be used as a part-name limit.
Same as R2527; in this data these are bryophyte gemmae.

PO lists 'needle-like leaf' as a synonym of vascular leaf, and the examples are conifer needle counts. Crystals and spines described as needle-like are handled by the quality rules (needlelike = subulate), so they do not appear as this bearer word. A part-name limit would not help here.
Plural of R2529; same reasoning.
No PO class exists for intersecondary veins. The parent leaf lamina vein is correct, as for basal vein and veinlet.
Same as R2494 and R2532.
